raw_response:
*(I think a bit, rub my hands, start talking as I see it.)*

Aiyo, what is there to think about? I been farming this land more than fifty years. What I did last year I do again this year. No need to change what already works. My wife and me, we're old now, can't do too much, but thirteen mu is not so much. Manageable.

Let me tell you how I handle it.

**Wheat first.** I plant wheat around Cold Dew time, early to middle October, after I clear the maize. Variety — I use the same seed the village store sells, whatever the local one is. Ji-mai something, I don't remember the number, my son reads it for me when he comes back. Costs maybe thirty, forty yuan a mu for seed. Some years I save my own seed from last harvest, but lately the new seed is better, I just buy.

Before planting I call the tractor man, he rotary-tills the whole thirteen mu in one morning, fifty yuan a mu. My old back can't push a plow anymore. Then I broadcast the base fertilizer myself — one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's the fifteen-fifteen-fifteen kind, blue bag from the agri-store. One bag is fifty jin, wait no, one hundred jin, fifty kilo. Then the tractor man works it in.

In spring when the wheat turns green and starts jointing, I spread urea. About a half bag per mu — urea is strong stuff, one bag covers two mu easy. If the wheat looks pale I do a bit more, if it looks dark green and tall I do a bit less. My eye knows.

Water — from the well. I irrigate three times usually. Winter water before it freezes, that one is important, old people always said winter water saves the crop. Then at jointing time if no rain. Then when the grain is filling, if no rain. If the sky gives water, I save the electricity money. Well pump is expensive, thirty yuan a mu each watering, and my legs hurt from walking the furrows all day.

Herbicide, yes, one time in spring for the grass. One small bottle covers the whole field, twenty yuan a mu maybe. No way I'm pulling weeds by hand at my age.

Harvest — the combine man comes in June, sixty yuan a mu, done in one afternoon. I sit by the road, watch the bags fill.

Last year I got — let me think — close to a thousand jin a mu, five hundred kilo. Some years better, some years worse. If the spring is dry and my irrigation can't keep up, maybe four hundred. I expect about the same this year, four hundred fifty, five hundred kilo, something like that.

**Then maize, right after wheat.** This is the hard part — the days between wheat harvest and maize planting are few, maybe five, six days. No time to plow. I hire the no-till seeder, thirty yuan a mu, and it plants maize straight into the wheat stubble with fertilizer together. I buy hybrid maize seed from the same store, sixty, seventy yuan a mu. Must be hybrid, the old kind gives nothing.

Base fertilizer with the seeder, one bag compound per mu same as wheat. Then at big flare stage, end of July, I topdress urea again, about half a bag per mu. If it hasn't rained, I irrigate one time, maybe two times. Maize is tougher than wheat, needs less water if the summer rains are normal.

Herbicide one time after planting, before the grass comes up. No insecticide usually, the corn borer is there but not so bad to spray.

Harvest in late September, combine man again, seventy yuan a mu. Last year maize was good, four hundred fifty, five hundred kilo a mu. I expect similar.

**Labor** — mostly me and the wife. She does the fertilizer spreading with me, watches the water when I irrigate. Thirteen mu is enough work for two old people but not too much. Maybe we each work twenty-five days in the fields across the whole year, not counting the hired machines. My son works in the city, sends money for the New Year, doesn't come home to farm.

**Money** — I have to be careful. Fertilizer goes up every year, seed goes up, electricity goes up. I can't apply the "best" amount like the young educated farmer next village over talks about. I apply what my hand knows and what my pocket allows. If I had more money I'd water the wheat one more time maybe. But you don't spend what you don't have.
